title: fix(objectql)!: a restrict reference refuses the delete of the record it protects even when the referencing row also cascades from it (#26718)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XKKhNWtvAHeAwPmZfHrR6PA)_

Fixes #26718

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the docs and skills already say a `restrict` refuses the parent delete while a referencing row exists (`content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`); this makes the runtime honour that on one more path, and nothing taught changes.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：按 id 删除父记录时，若某条明细既通过 master_detail 归属该父记录、又用 `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` 引用同一父记录（或级联更深一层的孙记录这样引用），现在先判定 restrict，返回 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`，什么都不删。
- **为什么改**：以前级联把这条明细算进“本次要删的集合”，集合内的行一律不触发 restrict，于是明细被静默级联删除，作者声明“不可删”的数据丢失（p1 数据丢失）。
- **风险与回滚**：只收窄这一种删除；集合外的 restrict、普通级联、set_null、必填 lookup 的升级 restrict 行为不变。回滚即撤销本 PR。#22305 定下的“同一父记录下兄弟之间的 restrict 不拦”保持原样，是否也要拦见 Acceptance notes 的待决问题。
- **先看**：`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` 的 `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade`（新增的写前判定）与 `collectCascadeDeleteSet` 里记录级联边的几行；`packages/runtime/src/cascade-delete-restrict-same-parent-real-driver.integration.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local src/cascade-delete-restrict-same-parent-real-driver.integration.test.ts`（先 build objectql），预期 7 条全绿；在 main 上同一文件 4 红。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`ObjectQL.cascadeDeleteRelations` (the by-id delete's referential walk, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) gains a read-only step between its two phases. After it collects the cascade set and before its first write, `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade` judges every AUTHORED `restrict` (the resolved behaviour of `cascadeRelationBehavior`: a `lookup`, `tree` or `master_detail` that declares `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'`) held by a member that the cascade reaches only THROUGH the record that restrict protects. Such a row refuses the delete with the walk's existing `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` envelope, built by one helper (`deleteRestrictedError`, lifted unchanged out of the walk), so the two refusals cannot drift.

"Reaches through" is read from the cascade edges the collection walk already probes, now recorded on the set (`CascadeDeleteSet.cascadeEdges`, `cascadeReachOf`). No new probe kind and no new read of the registry: the step probes a restrict relation only when its object has a member in the reach of the protected record.

## Why — where the ordering lives and why the cascade won

Re-checked on `origin/main` `c8583f80`. The card's suspected site holds: the walk is `cascadeDeleteRelations` → `collectCascadeDeleteSet` (phase 1) → `walkReferencingRelations` (phase 2) in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`. Two things let the cascade win:

1. **The #22305 exemption.** Phase 2 judged `restrict` only against rows OUTSIDE the cascade set (`dependents.filter(… !cascadeSetHas(cascadeSet.members, …))`). The child is in the parent's set by its own master_detail, so its restrict lookup was never asked, in either field order.
2. **Order inside the walk.** Each relation was judged as the field loop reached it, so with the master_detail declared first the child was already deleted when the restrict relation was probed.

Judging the restricts before the first write removes both. The #22305 rule itself stays for a row the cascade reaches through ANOTHER record (two details of one account, one restricting the other): the account's delete removes both.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/cascade-delete-restrict-same-parent-real-driver.integration.test.ts` (new): real `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 on disk), through the protocol's `deleteData` (the method `DELETE /api/v1/data/:object/:id` serves) and `deleteManyData` (the bulk door). The card's shape in both field orders, the bulk door, a grandchild holding the restrict; controls: the two fields at different parents, a plain master_detail, the parent deleting once the child is gone. Row counts are read out of the driver.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-sibling-restrict.test.ts` (new section, the #22305 file and its rollback-capable driver): the same shapes plus a grandchild restricting the member above it (refused from the root and directly alike), each asserting no write reached the driver; two controls. Every pre-existing #22305 pin in the file is unchanged and green.

## Acceptance notes

- **Open question for the seat (not decided here).** The triage ruling reads "a restrict on any path refuses the delete". The #22305 triage ruling, pinned in `engine-cascade-delete-sibling-restrict.test.ts` ("an AUTHORED restrict between two members does not refuse"), exempts an authored restrict held by a SIBLING member: deleting an account removes a quote and the contact the quote restricts, both details of the account. This PR keeps that pin and refuses only the rows reached through the record the restrict protects, which covers the card's shape, the grandchild case and the reverse field order. Whether the sibling case should refuse too is a reversal of the #22305 pin and is left to the seat; it is a one-line change in the new step (drop the reach filter for authored restricts). Measured producers: hotcrm (`afdf9a0`) declares authored restricts only on `crm_event_attendee.crm_event` and `crm_campaign_member.crm_campaign`, whose targets are never cascade members together with those rows, and this repo ships one, `sys_business_unit.parent_business_unit_id`; none of them meets either rule's changed case.
- **The bulk door shares the walk.** `deleteManyData` deletes by id, row by row, through `engine.delete`, and refuses the same row (pinned). The engine's PREDICATE delete (`multi: true` with a non-id `where`) runs no referential walk at all, by its documented contract (the `cascadeDeleteRelations` docblock, and `engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` "opens no transaction when … the delete is by predicate"); it is unchanged here and not reached by this card.
- **Required-lookup escalation unchanged.** A required lookup's `set_null`, refused as `restrict` because it cannot be cleared, still steps aside for a row the cascade deletes (#22305 "a member holding a required lookup to the ROOT does not refuse the root", green).
- **Cost.** One extra probe per authored restrict relation per member, only when the restricting object has a member in that member's cascade reach; the walk already probed the same relation.
- No save-time refusal of the combination was added (that would be a `packages/spec` card). No `ui/**`, no `packages/spec/**`.
- Overlapping open PR measured before opening: #26792 (engine split cut 16, the validate body) touches `engine.ts` in a different region.
